episodes.title: The One-Person Biotech | OpenAI Life Sciences
episodes.description: What happens when scientists are no longer limited by human attention? OpenAI’s Joy Jiao and Ashoka Rajendra join a16z’s Jay Rughani and Jorge Conde to discuss how AI and thousands of parallel agents could reshape drug discovery and development. They trace OpenAI’s life sciences work from scientific reasoning to the acquisition of Orchestra Bio, and how agents could search biological data, manage clinical trials, and navigate regulatory and manufacturing workflows. They also discuss AI’s role in solving difficult diagnoses and a future where a single person could potentially launch and advance multiple biotech programs. episodes.title: Rothy's: Roth Martin. The Art Dealer Who Built a $1B Shoe Brand from Plastic Bottles
episodes.description: Roth Martin was running a San Francisco design gallery when he and Stephen Hawthornthwaite decided to make a better women's shoe. Neither had worked in footwear. Their idea: a soft, comfortable flat that could do for shoes what technical fabrics (think: lululemon) had done for clothing. Getting there took six years, $1 million of Roth's own money, and long stretches away from his wife and four children. After a failed manufacturing effort in Maine, Roth moved production to China. But just as Rothy's launched and sales took off, a factory disaster threatened to unravel everything. episodes.title: What a Town Full of Vibecoders Says About the Chinese Economy
episodes.description: According to Stanford's AI Index, 84% of people surveyed in China say they are optimistic about AI. In the US, by contrast, 38% of those surveyed say they are optimistic. That's a big gulf in enthusiasm, and you can see it borne out in the stories you read. While in the US we hear about AI doomsday scenarios, in China, you'll hear about grandmas who are obsessed with using OpenClaw. episodes.title: 10億円調達のPlanet Savers、なぜ一度に集めない？
episodes.description: 本エピソードでは、直近で10.8億円を調達したPlanet Saversや15億円調達のWyLなど、大型資金調達のニュースが相次ぐスタートアップ市場の舞台裏に迫ります。 成長に多額の資金が必要なら、なぜ最初からまとめて集めないのか。その鍵を握るのが「バリュエーション（企業価値評価）」と「株式の希薄化」です。事業実績が乏しい初期に多額の資金を集めると投資家に渡す持分比率が過大になり、創業者の持ち分が大きく薄まってしまいます。そのため、シードからシリーズA、Bへと段階ごとにマイルストーンを達成し、企業価値を引き上げながら分割して調達を進めるのが定石です。 さらに、出資（エクイティ）だけに頼らず、融資やベンチャーデットを柔軟に組み合わせる「ファイナンスミックス」の重要性についても整理。資本政策の成否を分ける調達サイクルや事業規模の考え方まで、最新の資金調達動向を深く読み解くためのポイントをわかりやすくお届けします。
